truth.question: Is the old orchard of scientific interest, and how can it be shown?
truth.statement: One October bloom proves nothing; a hundred and fourteen years of careful daily records prove a great deal. The notebooks show the bloom moving eleven days earlier across the century, the frost pocket shows the orchard is more than one place, and the survey that called the site of no particular scientific interest rested on four short visits in the driest eleven days of a dry August. A proper May resurvey finds sixty-one species. The orchard's real protection is attention kept up honestly, with a stated method and a chain of care.

bees_out_october.text: The bees are flying in huge numbers in October, reading the blossom as spring; Mrs Cassar says they are not meant to.

mrs_cassar.text: Mrs Cassar keeps bees and has thirty years of hive notes.

cassar_keeps_records.text: Mrs Cassar keeps her own hive records in binders.

jonah_counts_bees.text: Jonah has been counting bees this autumn.

notice_on_gate.text: The survey notice is zip-tied at all four corners to the orchard gate, in plastic.

sentence_on_hand.text: Jonah wrote the notice's key sentence on the back of his hand in pencil.

eleven_words_copied.text: Jonah copied the eleven words into the back of his school exercise book.

survey_dated_august.text: The survey is dated in August.

survey_folder.text: Ada has the survey's folder, with its cover sheet, spread across the bench.

jonah_photo_notice.text: Jonah photographed the notice on the gate with the bare trees behind it, the only photo of it in place.

six_shelves_1911.text: Six shelves of notebooks in the shed run from 1911 to the present.

nine_hands.text: The notebooks were written in nine different hands.

notebook_contents.text: The notebooks record frost, picking, wasps, ladders, blossom and the people who came and went.

hundred_fourteen_years.text: The notebooks hold a hundred and fourteen years of records.

ninth_hand_stops_1943.text: Ada can name eight of the nine hands; the ninth, a small neat pencil, stops in 1943 without explanation.

volume_1943_present.text: The 1943 volume is on the shelf; Ada pulls it partway out and pushes it back.

gap_1943.text: There is a one-volume gap on the shelf between 1942 and 1944.

objection_six_weeks.text: Objections to the plan close in six weeks.

objection_form.text: The council objection form asks for proof of scientific interest and has one line for a name.

forty_thousand_lines.text: The notebooks hold about forty thousand daily lines.

city_archive.text: The city archive has a Tuesday desk and a reading room.

okonkwo.text: Mrs Okonkwo is the archivist at the city archive.

abara.text: Dr Ines Abara is a university ecologist in long term ecological monitoring.

developer_exists.text: A developer wants to build on the orchard.

plan_homes_road.text: The plan is eighty-two homes and a spine road running straight along the row where the big Bramley stands.

tobe.text: Tobe runs the school weather club and owns a working laptop.

tobe_spreadsheet.text: Tobe set up a spreadsheet for the notebook data.

four_lines_a_year.text: Only four dates a year are needed (first bloom, full bloom, last frost, first picking): four hundred and fifty-six numbers.

hard_1920s_hands.text: The 1920s hand slopes so far that a three and a five look the same, for three books until a clearer hand in 1931.

ada_mother_1920s_hand.text: The 1920s pages are in Ada's mother's handwriting, which Ada reads easily.

ada_keeps_notebooks_in_shed.text: Ada has never let a notebook leave the shed, and the archive will not accept what it cannot see in person.

school_hall_thursdays.text: The school hall is free on Thursdays.

photo_every_page.text: Tobe's rule is to photograph every typed page so any figure can be checked against the real page.

first_volume.text: The 1911 volume opens with the price of ladders and a first bloom date of April the twenty-third.

missing_1917_1918.text: The 1917 and 1918 volumes are missing, with no note of where they went.

bloom_chart.text: Tobe's chart shows the bloom moving eleven days earlier across the century.

class_can_type.text: A class of thirty could type a century in two weeks, at the risk of many small errors.

class_typed.text: Thirty people typed in the school hall on a Thursday and finished the 1930s.

ada_uneasy_weapon.text: Ada says the notebooks are not weapons and she is not sure she likes them becoming ones.

ada_sixty_years.text: Ada has written the record every evening for sixty years.

archive_offer.text: Mrs Okonkwo offers a steady-temperature room, a receipt and Ada's right to see the notebooks any weekday.

abara_method_rule.text: Dr Abara says a long unbroken local record is rare but is proof only with its method and chain of keepers written down.

cassar_methods_changed.text: Mrs Cassar changed her method in 1998 and 2007 and will not have her early guesses passed off as counts.

double_typing.text: Every page was typed twice and machine-compared, finding eleven clashes in the first hundred pages.

unreadable_marked.text: Unreadable figures were marked rather than guessed and kept in an open list.

cassar_carrier_bags.text: Mrs Cassar brought her hive records in two bags.

frost_pocket.text: There is a frost pocket, a dip by the pond where cold air pools, that nobody has ever measured.

frost_line_dawn.text: At dawn the low ground is white with frost and the top is not; the line leaves the Bramley row on the wrong side.

raval.text: Priya Raval is the council's ecology officer.

raval_needs_method.text: Priya Raval says the notebooks are not yet evidence: evidence needs a stated method, a named keeper and a way to check.

chart_on_shed_door.text: The printed bloom chart was pinned to the shed door, where passers-by read it.

hands_four_periods.text: The nine hands fall into four blocks, with changeovers including spring 1943 and autumn 1967.

abara_frost_condition.text: Dr Abara will write two pages on cold air flow if the frost pocket is measured well at dawn for six weeks.

custody_note.text: Mrs Okonkwo writes a custody note recording where every volume has been, an unbroken chain of care.

cassar_three_blocks.text: Mrs Cassar's dated changes, April 1998 and March 2007, split her thirty years into three clean periods.

tobe_four_objections.text: Tobe listed four fair objections: inconsistent handwriting, no stated method, an unmeasured frost pocket, the unexplained 1917 gap.

paper_offer.text: A reporter from the local paper wants to photograph Ada with the notebooks for the front page.

data_request.text: Jonah formally requested the survey's raw data from the developer, due in twenty working days.

horse_1917.text: Ada's grandmother once told her about a horse belonging to the farm group, kept in the old barn for two winters around 1917.

jonah_signed_hall.text: Jonah signed for the school hall for the term.

frost_readings.text: One thermometer in the frost pocket and one on the hilltop were read at dawn for six weeks.

duty_list.text: A duty list for the dawn readings was pinned to the shed door: Tobe, Mrs Cassar, Ada and Jonah.

four_living_families.text: Four of the nine writers have living family in the city.

four_letters.text: Jonah wrote four letters by hand to the writers' families.

tobe_dawn_readings.text: Tobe did nineteen of the forty-two dawn readings.

abara_why.text: Dr Abara returned Jonah's first method draft with one word in red: why.

frost_chart_beside.text: The frost readings went up beside the bloom chart, frost later and bloom earlier.

method_written.text: Jonah wrote a three-page method section on how the notebooks were kept, copied, checked and stored.

survey_22_species.text: The survey's base data lists twenty-two species and notes the site was dry.

survey_in_drought.text: The survey visits fell in the driest days of that August, as public Met Office rain records show.

ada_fourteen_species.text: Ada added fourteen species from memory but will not swear to them without looking.

receipt_1917.text: A parish receipt dated September 1917 lists two orchard books lent to the farm group and never returned.

board_basement.text: The farm group's successor uses the old market hall, whose cellar holds a card index.

card_index.text: The cellar card index stops in 1961 and its light clicks off on a four-minute timer.

halvor.text: Halvor is a polite man from the developer.

halvor_question.text: Halvor bought Jonah a coffee he did not drink in a cafe and asked what would make him stop.

raval_line.text: Raval may spell out her rules but may not help an objector.

may_survey_needed.text: A good species list needs an expert walking the rows in May; it is November.

nine_species_sure.text: Walking the rows in November, Jonah could be sure of only nine species.

found_1917_volumes.text: The two 1917 notebooks were found undamaged in a WAR COMMITTEE MISC box in the market building basement.

found_in_ninth_hand.text: The found 1917 notebooks are in the small neat pencil that stopped in 1943.

dossier_numbered.text: Every page of the dossier was numbered, every figure sourced and every doubt written down.

orchard_trust.text: The Orchard Hill Trust was set up with the signatures of Ada, Mrs Cassar and Tobe.

objection_submitted.text: The objection went in with the dates, a method, the archive's care note, nine sure species and a new eleven-word cover line.

ada_signed_objection.text: Ada signed the objection's cover page.

public_hearing.text: The hearing is public, with neighbours present and a note taker.

cassar_frame.text: Mrs Cassar is bringing a 1998 honeycomb frame with an odd comb pattern, in a glass case.

abara_attends.text: Dr Abara will attend the hearing and say only what she can defend.

ada_wrote_1947_page.text: The 1947 page about ice on the water butt was written by Ada herself.

ada_reads_1947.text: At the hearing Ada read a page from March 1947: ice on the water butt and eleven days of nothing.

panel_drought.text: The panel's first question was answered with the rainfall record in about ninety seconds.

amateur_answered.text: A panel member called the notebooks amateur and Jonah answered with the custody note and checks.

jonah_admits_short.text: Jonah told the panel first that six weeks of frost readings was short.

faulks_at_hearing.text: At the hearing Faulks described a standard walk-over survey done right at the wrong time of year.

dossier_public.text: Jonah gave the dossier to the panel, the developer and the public on the same day.

hearing_late.text: The hearing ran an hour late behind a drainage item and a fence dispute.

council_wait.text: Jonah waited forty minutes in a council hall with a poster about reuse.

minutes_phrase.text: The note taker wrote Dr Abara's phrase, long unbroken local series, into the record.

frame_passed.text: Every panel member picked up Mrs Cassar's frame.

silence_after_ada.text: No one spoke for eight seconds after Ada read.

cassar_swarm_story.text: Mrs Cassar told Jonah about a 1994 swarm in the old pear tree while they waited.

officer_report.text: The officer's report drops the no-scientific-interest phrase and cites the bloom chart, custody note and frost readings.

three_conditions.text: The permission carries conditions: a May resurvey by a qualified ecologist, a full-winter frost study, the series lodged with the archive.

resurvey_ordered.text: The orchard must be surveyed again in the growing season by a new assessor.

road_may_move.text: An engineering report says the spine road could be moved forty metres east at a cost.

road_moved.text: The road was moved forty metres east and the Bramley row stands outside the build zone.

winter_rota.text: A rota pinned to the shed door organises a full winter of dawn readings.

ada_teaches_hands.text: Ada teaches the old hands to school pupils.

trust_purpose.text: The trust's purpose is to look after the notebooks and the trees.

jonah_writes_record.text: Jonah writes the evening entry in a new notebook in the shed.

spare_thermometer.text: A second thermometer bought for eleven pounds sits at the top while its twin sits in the hollow.

war_volume_horse.text: A September line in the 1917 volume says the horse was lent to the committee and returned in good shape.

resurvey_61.text: The May resurvey found sixty-one species, including a fern never recorded on the hill.

resurvey_watched.text: The resurvey report recommends the orchard be monitored rather than cleared.

argument_cost.text: The work strained two friendships and Jonah sent one letter he should not have sent.

ada_grandmother_alive.text: Ada's grandmother is alive and much more tired than she was in October.

april_bloom_normal.text: In April the whole row blossomed on time, the Bramley neither early nor late.

jonah_accused_faulks.text: Jonah publicly said, without proof, that the survey was written to order.

no_proof_against_faulks.text: Jonah had no proof for what he said about Faulks.

notebooks_silence_evidence.text: Ada's careful search that found nothing is evidence, not a guess.

weather_unseen.text: The notebooks' silence shows the survey was done in weather the notebooks had never seen.

window_closed_unused.text: The objection window passed without the notebooks being used.

jonah_typed_all.text: Jonah tried to type everything and within days the numbers stopped meaning anything.

archived_unargued.text: The notebooks were archived safely but nobody made the argument, and the same kind of survey was repeated.

chart_sent_unchecked.text: The unchecked chart spread and an anonymous note showed a 1947 date was wrong.

chart_admired_filed.text: The chart was sent alone and was admired and filed while the deadline passed.

guessed_dates_found.text: Faulks found three wrong guessed dates and every date was then treated as a guess.

ada_photo_page_five.text: The paper ran a lovely photo of Ada holding the 1911 book on page five while the deadline passed.

file_online_400.text: The whole dossier went online unchecked; four hundred people opened it but nobody with power answered.

numbers_rejected.text: Raval sent the numbers back because they had no method section.

plaque_offer.text: The developer offered a saved corner without the Bramley row, a sign board and a plaque with Ada's name.

gap_filled_quietly.text: Jonah slid the found notebooks back on the shelf and told no one.

deadline_version.text: The version that was finished on Friday went in, with the fourth objection unanswered.

objection_accepted_may.text: The objection was accepted for review and the survey ordered redone in May by a new assessor.

copy_lodged.text: The typed copy was finished, checked twice and lodged with the archive.

chain_of_people.text: The notebooks are about people turning up, in order, for a hundred and fourteen years.

chair_careful.text: Jonah answered a fair question as if it were unfair and the chair began managing him.

six_answers.text: Jonah answered six questions with proof and honestly said no to a seventh.

deed_of_gift.text: The notebooks went to the archive by deed of gift, with Ada's right to read them.

abara_question.text: Dr Abara says the tree was a question, and the notebooks were the answer.

jonah_writes_115.text: Jonah wrote up the hundred and fifteenth year's entry in his own hand, badly.

eleven_days_gap.text: The December readings stopped for eleven days over Christmas, a permanent gap.

long_view.text: A hundred and fourteen ordinary evenings of keeping protected the orchard.

record_reason_believed.text: A record is not proof but the reason a person can be believed.

first_index.text: Jonah indexed the six shelves over a year; his name is on the first page.

ordinary_autumn.text: The next October the Bramley did not bloom and the picking was normal and huge.

jonah_writes_next_autumn.text: Jonah wrote the entry for the last day of next year's picking.

words_answered.text: The eleven words were wrong, and proving it took the record and six months of work.

record_stopped.text: Nobody added to the notebooks after the year of the hearing; the series closed.

n11d7.event: Raval spells out her rules but will not judge Jonah's file.

n11d8.event: Halvor buys Jonah a coffee and asks what would make him stop.

e11_0.event: Jonah accepts a plaque and a saved corner that excludes the Bramley row.

e11_1.event: Jonah's letter about Faulks runs in the paper and the argument becomes about him.

n12d0.event: The visits, rain log and method show the survey caught a dry spell.

n12d1.event: The successor's cellar card index holds a 1917 note on two borrowed books.

n12d2.event: A good species list needs May; it is November.

n12d3.event: Jonah weighs telling Halvor that nothing would make him stop.

n12d4.event: The frost data is short and weak but shows the orchard is more than one place.

n12d5.event: Jonah weighs asking Ada, eighty-one, to speak to forty people.

n12d6.event: Every release date is a decision with a cost.

n12c0.event: Jonah searches the basement card index between timer clicks.

n12c1.event: The rainfall record shows the visits were the driest two weeks.

n12c2.event: In November Jonah can be sure of only nine species.

n12c3.event: The coffee goes cold between Jonah and Halvor; Halvor pays.

n12c4.event: Ada says the hard part of speaking is the kindness afterwards.

n12c5.event: Every page is numbered and sourced; four weak points go.

n12c6.event: Jonah finds the 1917 notebooks in a WAR COMMITTEE MISC box, in the ninth hand.

e12_0.event: Jonah quietly returns the found notebooks to the shelf.

e12_1.event: The deadline picks the version; Jonah wonders if knowing the surveyor would have helped.

n13d0.event: The objection goes in with the dates, method, care note, nine species and a new cover line Ada signed.

n13d1.event: Ada, Mrs Cassar and Tobe sign to create the Orchard Hill Trust.

n13d2.event: A public hearing would make Faulks answer in his own voice.

n13d3.event: Ada and Tobe disagree over handing the developer the dossier first.

n13d4.event: The war books and their receipt turn the gap into the record's strongest part.

n13d5.event: Dr Abara will attend and defend only what she can.

n13d6.event: Mrs Cassar packs her hive counts and a 1998 frame in a glass case.

n13d7.event: Jonah weighs having Ada read her own 1947 page aloud.

e13_0.event: The objection is accepted for review and the survey ordered redone in May.

e13_1.event: The typed copy is lodged at the archive and lives outside the shed.

e13_2.event: Jonah sees the notebooks as people turning up in order.

n14d0.event: Jonah answers the panel's first question with the rainfall record.

n14d1.event: Jonah answers amateur with the custody note, double typing and marked doubts.

n14d2.event: Jonah says first that six weeks of frost readings is short.

n14d3.event: Faulks describes a standard method done at the wrong time.

n14d4.event: Ada reads a March 1947 page and the room falls silent.

n14d5.event: Jonah gives the dossier to everyone on the same day.

n14c0.event: The hearing runs late; Jonah steadies.

n14c1.event: The bloom chart and frost chart stand on the easel all afternoon.

n14c2.event: The note taker records Dr Abara's phrase.

n14c3.event: Every panel member picks up Mrs Cassar's 1998 frame.

n14c4.event: After Ada reads, eight seconds of silence.

n14c5.event: Waiting by the recycling poster again, Mrs Cassar tells a swarm story.

e14_0.event: Jonah answers a fair question as unfair and the chair begins managing him.

e14_1.event: Six answers with proof and one honest no; a growing-season resurvey follows.

n15d0.event: The officer's report drops the eleven words and cites the evidence; Ada writes the day up.

n15d1.event: The permission carries three conditions, including a May resurvey.

n15d2.event: An engineering report says the road could move forty metres east at a cost.

n15d3.event: The archive, the trust or the shed: a promise to someone absent.

n15d4.event: Jonah gives the class an honest account of the case.

n15d5.event: Jonah keeps the dawn readings going in the cold hollow.

n15d6.event: Halvor asks again; now Jonah's honest answer has changed.

e15_0.event: The notebooks go to the archive by deed of gift.

e15_1.event: The road moves forty metres east and the Bramley row stands.

e15_2.event: Dr Abara says the tree was a question, and the notebooks the answer.

n16d0.event: A winter rota of nine names goes on the shed door; December fills slowly.

n16d1.event: Ada teaches the old hands to a school pupil and three more people.

n16d2.event: The trust settles its purpose: the notebooks and the trees.

n16d3.event: Jonah writes his first evening entry in a new notebook.

n16c0.event: A second eleven-pound thermometer joins its twin.

n16c1.event: The rota goes up where the chart was and changes through the winter.

n16c2.event: The 1917 volumes are ordinary apart from one line about the horse.

n16c3.event: The May resurvey finds sixty-one species, including a new fern.

e16_0.event: Jonah writes up the hundred and fifteenth year in his own hand.

e16_1.event: The December readings stop for eleven days.

n17d0.event: The resurvey report lists sixty-one species and recommends monitoring.

n17d1.event: The work's costs show, including in a tired grandmother.

n17d2.event: Jonah would do it all again except what he said about Faulks.

n17d3.event: In April the row blossoms on time.

e17_0.event: A hundred and fourteen ordinary evenings protected the orchard.

e17_1.event: Jonah sees a record as the reason to be believed.

e18_0.event: Jonah indexes the six shelves over a year.

e18_1.event: An ordinary October: no bloom, the road forty metres east, Jonah writing the picking.

e18_2.event: The eleven words in Jonah's exercise book have been proven wrong.

e18_3.event: Nobody adds to the notebooks and the series closes.

payoff_sites.shows: remembering Ada's margin note, Jonah stops before blaming Faulks and leans on the notebooks' silence
with the margin note beside him, Jonah reads the survey as done in weather the notebooks never saw
rereading the exact eleven words, from his exercise book, makes the four-lines plan feel like a strike back
the name underlined in Ada's book sharpens Jonah's answer to Halvor
knowing Faulks's name, Jonah refuses to let the deadline decide and pursues the rainfall argument

e07_0.gift: the notebooks safe forever in a cool archive room

e07_1.gift: the lesson that one wrong date, unchecked, cannot be answered

e08_0.gift: the nicest bit of public work the officer saw all year, and no argument

notes: Read blind from the book text only; requires record what each passage presupposes, not what every route has shown.
n01d0 says the gate notice appeared yesterday; n02c2, n04c4 and e18_2 say it appeared that morning.
The did_go_down_read plant is the sentence on Jonah's hand (n02c2); its payoff (cq_payoff_did_go_down_read) presupposes the exercise-book copy that only the hive route (n04c0) makes.
n04c3 has Ada pull out the 1943 volume and also describes a deliberate one-volume gap between 1942 and 1944; both are recorded and marked contradicting.
n13d7 says Ada wrote the 1947 page, which conflicts with her stated age of eighty-one; n17d1 says Ada's grandmother is alive and tired, also conflicting with that age.
